concept: JetUP explainer #9, 'What "copying" really means', for How it works 'What "copying" really means' (/jetup/how-it-works/#copy) and get-started part 5 'Connect Sonic AI'. 16:9, 1920x1080, 25 fps, captions burned in, the JetUP logo disc (never MTG's photo), the series' glass style, only the four signature sounds. It answers the question every new member has about copy trading, 'What gets copied, and what stays yours?', with one everyday South African picture built piece by piece: a cooking class, drawn as a community-hall class with enamel pots on two-plate stoves. The chef at the front is Sonic AI (his hat badge); your own pot, with your name plate, is your own account (an MT5 account at TAG Markets, in your name), with your money in it; every other table has its own pot. In a class you copy each step with your own spoon; the twist is that you don't even lift the spoon, because the lime CopyX line carries the strategy's trades into your account automatically, and you don't pick the trades. What stays yours: your own account, and your choices (the strategy, how much to put in and when to stop, in the site's own words, with no exit rule added), with Sonic's record on Myfxbook to look at first, then his recorded 'Read the terms.' and the fee in his recorded words (a thirty percent performance fee, taken from profits only) on one enlarged row of his real CopyX screen. A fresh re-hook, 'Want to see it for yourself?', opens the last picture: your pot has a glass lid, the MetaTrader 5 app, where your investor password lets you watch every trade, read only. A two-column recap answers both halves of the hook in custody words ('your money stays in your own account', never 'stays yours'), then 'Simple, right? Now it's your turn', tap any Join JetUP button, the fixed signature ending and 'Next: the 70/30 split'. It shows what copying does, what you control and how you watch it; it does not retell who is who (explainer #2's minibus taxi) or what Sonic AI trades (explainer #1). Voice: 5 recorded body lines and the 4 shared lines (0 credits) plus 8 new lines in MTG Master Voice V3 (729 characters, 743 with the blank-line breaks, one request, 1 credit; 44 at the check on 13 Nov 2026, 43 after; only after MTG approves). No new line says 'Jet Up', 'Copy X', 'Sonic AI' or 'TAG'; line 7 carries V3's first 'MetaTrader five' and sends 'read-only' with a hyphen (both checked by ear before cutting). Body about 79 s to the end of the Join line at the V3 pace measured on #8 (89 s at most by the 2.6 words per second rule), hook to 'Now it's your turn' about 71 s, total about 2:05 (2:02 to 2:16). Plan only: nothing is recorded, rendered or published.
picture: A cooking class (spoken 'a cooking class'), drawn as a community-hall cooking class in the series' glass style: rows of tables with enamel pots on two-plate stoves, and the chef at the front in a plain apron and a white hat. Built one piece at a time; each part keeps its colour and label in every scene (the chef and his counter gold; your pot, its name plate and the CopyX line lime; the glass lid clear). The chef at the front = Sonic AI, the strategy: he makes the moves, and his hat badge reads 'Sonic AI · the strategy' (no gold bar or XAU label: what Sonic trades is explainer #1's job). Each stir he makes = a trade. Your own pot on your own table, with your name plate = your own account, an MT5 account at TAG Markets in your name (the plate reads 'Your account · TAG Markets · in your name'; MT5 appears only in the captions of the recorded line, because the lid is the app). The ingredients in your pot = your money, which stays in your own account. The other tables, each with its own pot and its own name plate = every member who connects Sonic AI copies into their own account: there is no shared pot. In a real class you copy each step yourself, with your own spoon. The twist: you don't even lift the spoon. The lime line labelled 'CopyX' from the chef's pot into yours, and fainter lines into every other pot = CopyX, TAG Markets' copy trading platform, which connects your account to the strategy, so the strategy's trades are copied into your account automatically. The spoon resting on its rest for the rest of the video = you don't pick the trades. Three numbered slots beside your table = your three choices: the strategy (which chef: SONIC, first in the CopyX list), how much to put in (an unmarked jug: the training uses 50, the screen's minimum is $10) and when to stop (your own raised hand: your call, in the site's own words, with no small line and no stop steps, because the facts give none). The glass lid on your pot = the MetaTrader 5 app: with your investor password you can watch every trade in your own account, read only (watch, not trade or withdraw). The proof is shown as the real thing, MTG's own CopyX screens, not forced into the picture: SONIC first in the list with 'Check the record yourself: Myfxbook', the fee on one enlarged row in the screen's own label (Performance Fee 30%, taken from profits only), and the eye icon where the investor password lives. Never shown, so the picture suggests no trade sizes, no timing, no exit rule and no results: no amounts or markings in any pot or jug, no stir drawn bigger or smaller than another (every stir is the same simple move), no two pots side by side to compare, no clock or timer, no 'live' or 'same time', nothing for 'when to stop' that switches, turns, flips or counts days (no switch, no knob, no calendar), no finished dish, tasting or score, no volume or heat knob, no flames or boiling over, no nonstop stirring (the chef stirs once, then rests), and no MT5 trade rows, balances or performance figures anywhere, cover included. The voice says only 'cooking class', 'chef', 'pot', 'spoon' and 'glass lid', so the drawing can change for free (for example a church cooking day).
why_it_works: 1) It opens on the two-part question people really have about copy trading, on screen from the first frame and in MTG's voice by about 3.5 s: 'What gets copied, and what stays yours?' Three empty numbered slots and a glinting glass lid open two visible loops, paid off when the slots fill with the three choices (about 33 to 40 s) and in the glass lid scene (about 52 to 61 s); two re-hooks ('And the twist?' at about 14 s and 'Want to see it for yourself?' at about 52 s, fresh words rather than the 'Don't take my word for it' that #2 and #8 already use) and the two returning questions (about 27 and 33 s) keep the loop alive, and the two-column recap answers both halves. 2) One everyday picture that shows copying itself, not who is who (that was #2's taxi): an original move (the chef's stir) copied into your own pot and into every other table's own pot. The mechanism is visible: the moves travel, your pot and your ingredients never move. 3) The twist 'you don't even lift the spoon' lands straight after the set-up, as a smile, not a promise; the mechanism follows in MTG's recorded voice (your MT5 account at TAG Markets in your name, then you connect a strategy through CopyX, while the chef's hat badge names Sonic AI), and the answer to the first half follows at about 27 to 28 s: the strategy's trades, into your account, automatically, and you don't pick the trades. 4) What stays yours is said in the site's own words, once and positively: your own account, and your choices (the strategy, how much to put in, when to stop), with SONIC first in the list shown on MTG's real CopyX screen, the training's 50 and the screen's $10 minimum as one small line, and when to stop in the site's own words, with no exit rule, time or steps added. 5) Trust without a single warning: look before you deposit (Myfxbook, no figures), read the terms (the fee, taken from profits only, on one enlarged row of his real screen), then 'Want to see it for yourself?' and the glass lid: MetaTrader 5 with the investor password, read only, on MTG's real eye icon, with no invented trade rows, balances or performance numbers. 6) Custody words only: 'your money stays in your own account' (the site's words), never 'your money stays yours'; under 'What stays yours?' only the name plate lights, never the money; the never-shown list keeps out anything that suggests trade size, timing, an exit rule or results. 7) One idea, one focal point at a time: what Sonic AI trades, the 70% share, where the 30% goes, Amplify, the loss limit, the one month minimum and the MetaTrader 5 set-up details stay with the other explainers and the pages, so 'Next: the 70/30 split' is the natural next question rather than a replay; every screen beat carries one crop and at most two short chips, readable on a phone. 8) It converts: a warm recap, 'Simple, right? Now it's your turn', and one action, the Join JetUP button tapped on screen. 9) Cheap and safe for his voice: 8 new lines, 729 characters, 1 credit; no new line says 'Jet Up', 'Copy X', 'Sonic AI' or 'TAG' (they stay in his banked voice); V3's first 'MetaTrader five' is checked by ear and speech-to-text before cutting, and 'read-only' is sent with a hyphen and checked by ear. Pictures weighed and dropped: a radio station and the radio at home (very everyday, but nothing in it is your money or 'how much to put in', and a broadcast suggests the same song at the same moment, a size and timing claim); a soccer club with a coach (a coach running your club is management, not copying, and wins, goals and a prize card read like results or betting); a dance class or choir (you make every move yourself); a driving instructor (a third transport picture); a mirror (South Africans link 'mirror trading' to a collapsed scheme); a braai master (he handles your meat, like handing over your money); a WhatsApp signal group (looks like the scams burned viewers fear); a carbon-copy receipt book, a photocopier or a pantograph (no choices, or a sizing claim). The runner-up was copying the teacher's notes from the chalkboard into your own exercise book: strong on 'copy' and read only, but no money and no 'how much', and copying at school can mean cheating.

scenes.name: What stays yours

On 'your choices' the slots move beside your table and fill on his words (three ticks): 1 'The strategy' (a chef's hat), small line 'SONIC, first in the CopyX list'; 2 'How much to put in' (an unmarked jug), small line 'The training uses 50 · the screen's minimum: $10'; 3 'When to stop' (your own raised hand: your call), with no small line and nothing that switches, turns, flips or counts days.
